why: Garage Claes sends hours by the 20th at noon. Sanne: "Their workshop planner closes that day, so later numbers are always guesses."
Garage Claes keeps the two company cars on the fleet manager list, we only update the payroll file when Claes confirms in writing. "Verbal changes caused two corrections."
Drukkerij Vermeulen pays salaries on the 27th, or the Friday before if it falls on a weekend, because their bank batch runs on Thursday afternoon.
Drukkerij Vermeulen pays the year-end premium with the November salary, not December. Owner Vermeulen wants it before the Sinterklaas weekend.
Hotel Ter Duinen has a cutoff of the 18th at 10:00 in summer because the night shifts are only closed by the duty manager that morning.
Hotel Ter Duinen stays on the paper-free meal voucher card from Edenred. Joris: "Staff eat on site, so the card at the staff canteen terminal was the only workable option."
Transport Maes issues eco-cheques in June on a Pluxee card. Drivers had asked for a card instead of paper because they lose paper vouchers in the cab.
Transport Maes sends driver allowance corrections late almost every month. We pay them in the next run and tell the owner in writing, no off-cycle payments.
During holidays Apotheek Lievens HR questions go to Emma first. Pharmacist Lievens only has two employees and does not want to call a general helpdesk.
Apotheek Lievens got mysdworx in September for payslips only. The leave request module waits until both employees have used the payslip part for two months.
Schoonmaak Peeters delivers its timesheets on the 19th by 16:00, because cleaning teams hand in paper sheets on the 18th and the office types them in the day after.
New Schoonmaak Peeters cleaners need the signed contract and a bank account number before the first day. Kobe: "Without it the first payslip slips a month."
IT Solutions Gent pays the home office allowance as a fixed amount per month. Decided with their HR lead so the monthly file has no variable lines.
IT Solutions Gent asked for a headcount and cost report by the 5th working day of each month, because their finance closes on the 8th.
Bouwbedrijf Willems has the cutoff on the 15th because foremen submit site hours every second Friday. Pieter keeps the 15th fixed to avoid arguments.
Nina took Bouwbedrijf Willems over from Alberic in August. Handover note: the foreman Dirk sends hours on WhatsApp, always ask him for an email copy.
Slagerij Hendrickx pays on the last working day of the month because the owner transfers from his own business account after the Saturday market.
Slagerij Hendrickx gives a year-end premium in the December run, paid in cash value as a gift voucher from the local shopping association only if the owner decides so by 1 December.
Restaurant De Gouden Leeuw closes the month on the 21st, because the restaurant is closed on Mondays and the manager does the hours then.
De Gouden Leeuw hires many students in summer. Alberic sends the owner a one-page checklist in May so contracts are signed before the first shift.
Tuinaanleg Goossens switched eco-cheques from Sodexo paper to a card in April, since the team leaders no longer wanted to carry envelopes to the sites.
Tuinaanleg Goossens sends no hours in January. We prefill from the planning spreadsheet and the owner approves by email, which saves a call every month.
Elektro Janssens vans are not company cars in the payroll file. Emma checked with the owner, so no car lines are needed for the technicians.
Elektro Janssens exports Protime on the first working day after month end, before 09:00. Thomas imports it before noon so the owner sees draft numbers the same day.
Kinderopvang Zonnebloem onboarding checklist: contract templates, bank details, medical check date, mysdworx invitation. Sanne: "Four items, one week, nobody forgets the medical date."
Kinderopvang Zonnebloem is closed between Christmas and New Year, so the December cutoff moves to the 17th. Director Peeters signed this off in October.
Autohandel Dierckx has a cutoff of the 22nd, because sales commission is only final after the last delivery of the month is registered.
Autohandel Dierckx commission corrections after cutoff are paid with the next month salary. Kobe told the finance manager and he agreed in an email.
Fietsenwinkel Pedaal pays on the 25th. The owner wants salaries in before the spring sale weekend, so April moves to the 24th.
Fietsenwinkel Pedaal staff get mysdworx on their phones only, nobody uses a PC there. Pieter made a short screenshot guide for the shop floor.
Modehuis Van Damme keeps meal vouchers on Pluxee because their shops in three cities already have the card reader account with that provider.
Modehuis Van Damme pays the year-end premium in the first December run, so shop staff have it before the Christmas shopping rush.
Advocatenkantoor Lambrecht wants every HR question in writing to one mailbox. Nina answers within one working day, and calls only when the partner calls first.
Advocatenkantoor Lambrecht asked for a quarterly salary cost split by partner and associate, delivered by the 10th of the month after the quarter.
Tandartspraktijk Mertens has one company car for the practice manager. Policy: she changes the car only at year start, so we do not rework the file mid-year.
Tandartspraktijk Mertens sends changes by the 20th at 17:00. Dentist Mertens does admin on Wednesday evenings, so we do not chase before then.
Houthandel Coppens has a cutoff on the 17th because the sawmill shifts end on the 16th and the foreman checks the clock sheets the morning after.
Joris handed Houthandel Coppens to Thomas in September. Note: the owner prefers phone calls before 09:00 and dislikes long emails.
Verpakkingen Aerts hands out eco-cheques in the June run on a card. HR manager Aerts chose the card to avoid the yearly paper delivery that was always late.
Verpakkingen Aerts uses Protime for the shift teams. Alberic imports the export on the 16th so night shift overtime is correct before the cutoff.
Bloemisterij De Roos pays on the 28th, or the 26th in May, because Mother Day week leaves no time to approve payments.
New staff at Bloemisterij De Roos start with a trial day. We only prepare the contract after the owner confirms the trial went well, so no empty contracts get filed.
Boekhoudkantoor Smets has a cutoff on the 12th, because the bookkeepers are busy with VAT returns from the 15th and need payroll done first.
Invoice questions from Boekhoudkantoor Smets go to Emma. They want one combined invoice per quarter, with a line per employee, not per payroll run.
Sanitair Wouters moved meal vouchers from paper to the Edenred card in March. Plumbers on the road found it easier to pay at lunch stops.
Sanitair Wouters company car changes go through the owner only. Thomas asked for a fixed rule after an employee sent a car order himself.
Wijnhandel Desmet pays the year-end premium on 15 December, because the busy period starts after that and the owner does not want payroll questions in the last week.
Wijnhandel Desmet cutoff is the 23rd. December is the exception, with the 14th, because the shop is open daily until Christmas.
Plantenkwekerij Verhoeven hires seasonal staff from March. Kobe asks the owner for the list of names by 1 March, so contracts exist before day one.
Plantenkwekerij Verhoeven rolls out mysdworx in two steps: office staff in October, greenhouse staff in January once the seasonal rush has ended.
Sanne owns the hospitality portfolio: Hotel Ter Duinen, Restaurant De Gouden Leeuw and Wijnhandel Desmet. Questions about these clients go to her first.
Joris owns the trades portfolio: Garage Claes, Elektro Janssens and Sanitair Wouters. He decided to keep them together because the cutoff dates are similar.
Alberic owns the manufacturing portfolio: Drukkerij Vermeulen, Verpakkingen Aerts and Houthandel Coppens until the September swap.
Pieter owns retail: Fietsenwinkel Pedaal, Modehuis Van Damme and Bloemisterij De Roos. He asked for retail because he likes the seasonal rhythm.
Emma owns the healthcare and care portfolio: Apotheek Lievens, Kinderopvang Zonnebloem and Tandartspraktijk Mertens.
Kobe owns the services portfolio: Schoonmaak Peeters, Autohandel Dierckx and Plantenkwekerij Verhoeven. Thomas covers when Kobe is away.
Nina owns the professional services portfolio: IT Solutions Gent, Advocatenkantoor Lambrecht and Boekhoudkantoor Smets, plus Bouwbedrijf Willems since August.
Thomas owns Transport Maes and Slagerij Hendrickx and the dedicated backup role. Everyone in the team can reach him by chat for urgent cutoff questions.
The weekly portfolio review is on Tuesday at 10:00 for 30 minutes. Sanne: "Tuesday works because Monday absorbs the weekend email and Wednesday is client call day."
In the Tuesday review each consultant names the one client with the highest risk this week. We decided on one name, not a list, so the meeting stays short.
Open points from the Tuesday review go into the shared notes the same day. Whoever raised the point writes it, so nobody has to ask who owns it.
When a cutoff is within three working days, that client goes first in the Tuesday review. Joris suggested it after a late hours file in spring.
Legal Watch alerts are triaged by Emma on Monday morning. She marks each alert as relevant for named clients, or archives it with a one-line reason.
If a Legal Watch alert touches a client directly, the portfolio owner emails the client within the week. We agreed that so clients hear it from us first.
Legal Watch alerts that need a change in payroll setup get a note in the weekly review. Alberic: "We want one person to say yes before any setup changes."
Nobody replies to a client about a Legal Watch alert before Emma has read it. This avoids mixed answers when two clients ask about the same topic.
Protime exports are saved in the client folder under the month name before import. If an import fails, the saved file shows whether the client or we caused the problem.
For Protime clients we compare total hours in the export with the totals on the client summary before importing. A mismatch goes back to the client the same day.
Thomas checks Protime exports for clients with night shifts first, since those have the most manual corrections and need a day of buffer.
We do not edit Protime exports by hand. Corrections are made in Protime by the client, so their own records stay equal to our payroll input.
Invoice questions from clients go to Emma, contract questions go to the portfolio owner, and questions about both go to Emma, who forwards the contract part.
Contract renewals are tracked by Nina in a sheet with the renewal date and the owner. She sends a reminder to the owner 60 days before the date.
Credit notes are only issued after the portfolio owner confirms the mistake was ours. Pieter proposed this after an invoice was credited too quickly.
The team keeps client notes in the shared knowledge base, not in personal mailboxes. Sanne: "When someone is ill, the notes must be findable without asking."
We use one shared chat channel for urgent cutoff questions and email for everything that needs a record. Kobe suggested it after missing a message in a private chat.
Client calendars with cutoff dates are shared in the team calendar with a colour per consultant, so colleagues see at a glance who is busy.
We checked a ticket tool for client requests and decided against it. For eight people, a shared mailbox with a clear owner per client is faster.
Standard rule: a correction received after cutoff is paid in the next run. Exceptions need the portfolio owner and a written confirmation from the client.
When a correction after cutoff is our mistake, we fix it in the next run and tell the client the same day. Alberic: "Clients forgive errors faster than silence."
Off-cycle payments for corrections are only done when the amount is large for the employee. The owner of the portfolio decides, and the client confirms by email.
Late corrections are logged with the date and the client reason, so at renewal time we can show a client how often it happened.
During summer holidays each consultant names a backup in the team calendar by 1 June. The backup reads the handover note for each client before the holiday starts.
Clients get the name of the backup and the dates one week before a consultant leaves. Nina sends the mail to all clients in the portfolio.
Over Christmas two consultants stay on call for cutoff questions. The rota is agreed in November, and the others do not answer client email.
Onboarding of a new client starts with a kickoff call within one week of signing. The portfolio owner leads, a second consultant takes notes.
We collect the cutoff date, pay date, meal voucher provider and contact for HR questions in the first call. Pieter: "These four items cause the most trouble later."
First payroll run of a new client is checked by a second consultant. Pieter or Thomas does this review, never the owner of the portfolio.
New clients get a parallel run for the first month where possible. We agreed it after a client found a mistake in the second month.
mysdworx is rolled out per client with a 30 minute demo for the contact person first. Employees get invited only after the contact person is comfortable.
We start every mysdworx rollout with payslips only. Leave requests and other modules follow after at least two months, once staff log in without help.
Kobe keeps a list of clients with mysdworx status in the shared notes, updated after each rollout, so the team knows whom to call for questions.
A handover note covers cutoff date, pay date, contact person, special agreements and open points. Anything else is optional, which keeps notes short.
Handover notes are written by the outgoing consultant and read by the incoming one in a short call. Sanne asked for the call because notes alone missed the tone.
After a handover the old consultant stays reachable for questions for four weeks. After that, the new owner is responsible alone.
In October each consultant asks clients when the year-end premium is paid. Answers go into the shared notes by the end of the month.
Clients that pay the year-end premium in December need amounts by the cutoff of the month before. Joris reminds them in the first week of November.
Eco-cheque provider is a client decision. We advise a card for clients with field staff, and paper only where the client has a stock of paper vouchers.
Meal voucher provider changes happen at the start of a month only. The client signs a short note, and we update the payroll setup before cutoff.
For company cars we ask the client for the fleet list once a year. Between lists, changes need an email from the person who signs the car contract.
Company car changes sent by employees directly are passed to the client contact first. Thomas: "The employee is not our client, the company is."
Employee HR questions that reach us directly are answered only when the client gave us written permission. Otherwise we refer to the client contact.
For clients without HR staff, the owner is the contact for HR questions. We note that in the client file so a new colleague does not call the wrong person.
Reporting deadlines requested by clients are written in the client file and added to the team calendar by the portfolio owner the same week.
Monthly cost reports go out on the second working day after payroll closes. Pieter set that date so clients can book salaries on time.
A change of pay date needs one full month notice from the client. Alberic set this rule because the bank batches are planned a month ahead.
When the pay date falls on a weekend, we pay on the Friday before unless the client wrote otherwise. Most clients prefer it that way.
Cutoff reminders go out three working days before the date, by email from the portfolio owner. Sanne: "A reminder on the day itself is useless."
Clients who miss a cutoff twice in a row get a call from the portfolio owner, not another email. Emma found that calls solve it faster.
Cutoff dates are moved only once per client per year for holidays. Beyond that, we ask the client to plan around the fixed date.
New mechanics at Garage Claes start on the first of the month only. Joris asked Claes for this so tool allowance and uniform are settled before the first payslip.
Drukkerij Vermeulen overtime from the night press run arrives a day late. We pay it in the next run and the production manager accepted that in writing.
Hotel Ter Duinen rolls out mysdworx to the housekeeping team in November, after the season. Sanne wanted a quiet period so staff have time to learn it.
Transport Maes cutoff is the 16th at 12:00. Tachograph data is only complete then, and the planner Maes checks it himself before sending.
Apotheek Lievens sends changes by the 21st. The pharmacist does the monthly schedule on the 20th, so earlier requests are always incomplete.
Schoonmaak Peeters has no meal vouchers because teams work split shifts at client sites. Kobe wrote this in the file after the owner asked twice.
IT Solutions Gent pays on the 25th with no weekend rule, because their bank pays out on the exact date and the staff expect that.
Bouwbedrijf Willems pays on the 5th of the following month. This was agreed when they signed and stays unless the owner asks for a change with a month notice.
Slagerij Hendrickx hires through the owner only. Thomas sends one contract per hire and waits for the signed copy before putting the employee in the payroll.
Restaurant De Gouden Leeuw pays a year-end premium in the January run, after the busy December weeks, so the manager knows the final results first.
Tuinaanleg Goossens pays on the 30th. Owner Goossens invoices clients at month end and wants money in his account before he pays staff.
Elektro Janssens technicians use mysdworx to download payslips. Emma showed the owner how to reset a password so he does not need to call us.
Kinderopvang Zonnebloem uses the Pluxee card for meal vouchers and loads it on the 1st. The director chose the card because loading is automatic.
Autohandel Dierckx pays the year-end premium in the December run, but only after the car stock count on 20 December is done, per the owner.
Fietsenwinkel Pedaal has a cutoff on the 20th. In spring it moves to the 18th because the workshop works overtime and the owner needs time to check it.
Modehuis Van Damme cutoff is the 19th at 15:00. The three shop managers send hours to head office on the 18th and head office combines them.
New staff at Advocatenkantoor Lambrecht are announced by the office manager at least ten days before the start date, so contract and mysdworx access are ready.
Tandartspraktijk Mertens uses mysdworx only for payslips. The assistants asked for it, and the dentist agreed after a short demo from Emma.
Houthandel Coppens keeps paper meal vouchers for the warehouse team. The owner said the staff prefers paper, and a change would need a vote.
Verpakkingen Aerts pays the year-end premium with the November salary. The union representative asked for this and management agreed in the autumn meeting.
Bloemisterij De Roos hands out eco-cheques in paper form in June, because the owner likes to give them personally in an envelope.
Boekhoudkantoor Smets hires interns each summer. Nina sends the intern checklist in May with contract, bank details and the start date.
Sanitair Wouters sends hours on the 18th by 11:00. The owner's wife does the admin on Tuesday and Thursday mornings only.
Wijnhandel Desmet staff are on mysdworx since September, payslips and leave requests. Sanne reports that the owner uses the leave overview every week.
Plantenkwekerij Verhoeven cutoff is the 22nd. In peak season, March to June, the owner sends hours weekly so the final month file is small.
When a client sends hours after cutoff, the portfolio owner answers the same day with the next run date. Pieter wants a clear date, not a vague promise.
A new consultant shadows the portfolio owner for two cutoff cycles before running a client alone. Sanne set it after her own first month.
Each client has one note with cutoff, pay date, contacts and special agreements. Whoever learns a new agreement updates the note that day.
Notes record who agreed and when, for example Owner Peeters by email on 12 March. Joris wants agreements to be traceable without searching mailboxes.
Urgent client requests are answered by the portfolio owner or the named backup within two hours on working days. Anything slower must be told to the client.
The day after the biggest cutoff, the team eats lunch together. Kobe organizes it. The point is a calm moment after a stressful week.
Once a month the Tuesday review ends with ten minutes about what went wrong. Emma: "We write down one fix per problem, not a list."
Twice a year the portfolio owner calls each client to ask what could be better. Notes go into the client note, not into a separate report.
Contract renewals are discussed in September for the next year. Nina prepares a summary of hours spent per client so the talk has numbers.
If a client disputes an invoice, the portfolio owner calls before Emma writes anything. We want the client to hear a person first.
The backup consultant may answer questions and prepare the run, but changes to agreements wait for the owner. Thomas wrote this rule down after a misunderstanding.
Requests for employee data from outside the client contact are not answered. The client contact has to ask, and we note the request in the client note.
For clients hiring staff from abroad, the portfolio owner asks for the start date six weeks ahead. The extra steps need time, said Alberic in the autumn meeting.
In the last week of November the team goes through a year-end checklist per client: premium, last cutoff, holiday dates and contact for January questions.
On the first Tuesday of January the review covers every client's new-year changes. Pieter asked for it after two clients missed a pay date change.
For clients with shift work, sick leave goes by phone to the manager and by email to us the same day. Kobe wrote this into three client notes.
